title: Disconnect during startup sends can bypass task/session cleanup
reasoning: The route increments the session connection count immediately after a successful handshake, but the cleanup finally block does not begin until line 139. The client-tool-manifest and remote-tool-catalog sends happen before that protected region. If either send raises because the client disconnected or the socket failed, cleanup_connection is skipped, so the per-user connection count is not decremented and end_session may never run for that connection. This can leak session state and leave subsequent cleanup decisions using a stale active-connection count.
recommendation: Move the try/finally to cover all post-handshake session mutation and startup sends, or wrap the startup sends in the same protected connection lifecycle block after increment_connection_count.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for startup send failures or disconnects between handshake completion and receive-loop entry.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a websocket route test where SafeWebSocket.send_json raises after increment_connection_count, then assert cleanup_connection runs and session_manager.decrement_connection_count/end_session are called as appropriate.
